docs.summary: One decoded raster: one per animation frame, icon entry, or mipmap level and array slice. The pixel memory is owned by the [`Image`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.Image) that produced it, so a span taken from a frame must not outlive it. Use [`CopyTo`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.ImageFrame~CopyTo) when it has to.
Width of this frame in pixels, which for an animation may be smaller than the canvas.
Height of this frame in pixels, which for an animation may be smaller than the canvas.
Bytes between the start of one row and the start of the next. Equal to the packed row length unless [`RowAlignment`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.DecodeOptions~RowAlignment) asked for padding.
Layout of the pixel data.
Left edge of this frame on the parent canvas.
Top edge of this frame on the parent canvas.
How long this frame is shown, zero for a still image.
What happens to this frame's region before the next frame is drawn.
How this frame combines with the canvas underneath it.
Mipmap level, zero being the full resolution image.
Array slice or cube map face, zero for a plain 2D texture.
Total bytes of pixel data, which is [`Stride`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.ImageFrame~Stride) times [`Height`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.ImageFrame~Height).
The pixel data, top row first. Valid only until the owning [`Image`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.Image) is disposed.
The pixel data as a `Memory<T>`, for the asynchronous and buffer-writer APIs that cannot take a span. Valid only until the owning [`Image`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.Image) is disposed.
One row of pixels.

docs.summary: Copies the pixels into a caller owned buffer, re-striding rows on the way. Pass the row pitch a graphics API reported and the rows land where its driver expects them.
docs.returns: False when the destination is too small; nothing is written in that case.

params.destination: Where to write. Must hold [`GetRequiredBytes`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.ImageFrame~GetRequiredBytes) bytes.
params.destinationStride: Bytes between rows in `destination`, or zero to use this frame's stride.

docs.summary: Bytes a [`CopyTo`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.ImageFrame~CopyTo) at the given row pitch needs.
